title: The energy spectrum: how energy and dissipation are distributed over wavenumber, and what the second-order correlations add
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Lectures 29 and 30 repeat material of the preceding chapter (L29 0-460 s: the inertial-range scales and T(l) = eps; L30 250-645 s: the N-point restatement). The chapter restates them in one paragraph each and cites that chapter by title only, because it was not committed when this chapter was written.

L30 slide f0022 prints the second factor of D_ij as U_j(x+r,t) - U_j(x+r,t); the next slide (f0027) and Kolmogorov's definition give U_j(x+r,t) - U_j(x,t). The chapter writes the corrected form and says so. (11.14) uses the velocity fluctuation u, not the slide's U, and the slide's word 'covariance' is replaced by 'second moment'; the slide's form agrees when the mean is uniform. The speech (L30 about 733 s) reads the slide as printed.

ASR: 'endpoint PDF' for N-point PDF (L30 about 260-640 s); 'mu' for nu in Re_L (L30 about 1467 s; slide f0050 writes nu); 'Competibular and Colcine' for Comte-Bellot and Corrsin (slide f0037 prints the names); 'Kormogorov', 'chromogram' for Kolmogorov; 'L22 equal to half of L33' at 1211-1225 s, self-corrected to L11 by the speaker; 'phi' for p and 'new' for nu in the power-law derivation (L29 940-1190 s). The chapter follows the slides.

L29 about 593 s: 'identical' for the collapse of spectra in Kolmogorov variables; the measured collapse holds above a wavenumber that decreases with the Reynolds number (Saddoughi 1993, p. 246, Figure 3, p. 245). The chapter states the qualified form.

L29 slide f0035 says p = 5/3 'is around the middle of the range (1,3)'; the midpoint is 2. The chapter reports the slide's wording and states that the convergence condition applies to unbounded power laws only.

L30 1557-1562 s: the lecturer says Re_lambda 'applies only to grid turbulence' and cannot be used for jets or channels; the slide (f0050) says it is 'traditionally used to characterize grid turbulence'. The chapter attributes the stronger statement to the lecturer and grades it (Saddoughi reports Re_lambda 600 and 1500 in a boundary layer).
L30 about 1520 s: 'purely theoretical' for the Taylor scale; slide f0050 says it has no clear physical interpretation but is well defined and often used. Attributed as a judgment.

L30 slide f0046 attributes eps = 15 nu u'^2/lambda_g^2 and the 'smallest eddies' interpretation to Taylor (1935). Taylor's paper was not obtained (see INDEX.md); the attribution is the lecture's. Kolmogorov (1941) eq. (14) gives eps = 15 nu a^2 and Saddoughi p. 237 writes the same with 'see Taylor 1935'.

Slide Figure 6.14 axes are read from a 1280-px frame (f0019); the printed y-axis label is E11(kappa1)/(eps nu^5)^(1/4). Saddoughi Figure 3 labels the same compilation E11(k1 eta)/(eps nu)^(1/2). Both are one-dimensional spectra; the chapter uses the slide's label.

The slide caption cites Saddoughi and Veeravalli (1994, J. Fluid Mech. 268), which was not obtained. All measured values come from Saddoughi (1993), the Annual Research Brief of the same group, checked on the page. The 'model spectra (Eq. 6.246)' of the caption are not treated (forward reference by title).

Slide Figure 6.6 (f0037) attributes f(r) in grid turbulence to Comte-Bellot and Corrsin (1971); not obtained; reported as attributed on the slide. The reading 'f decays more slowly with r/M farther downstream' is from the figure as shown.

Saddoughi Figure 3: the statement that data of lower R_lambda leave the common curve at progressively larger k1 eta, 'about 1e-2 for the lowest values', is read from the figure; the text statement (p. 246) is the quoted one.

Saddoughi p. 247 C = 1.5 +/- 0.1: the isotropic compensated lines were drawn with the classical C = 1.5 and the data 'agree well'; the dissipation (accurate to 10 %) comes from the isotropic relation. The chapter reports this dependence.
Yeung and Zhou: Sreenivasan's survey value 0.53 +/- 0.055 and Zhou's C = 1.5 are reported by them (report p. 2); the original papers were not opened. Report pages: PDF page minus 2.

Kerr (1983): value, sign and the strain statement checked on the page (pp. 15, 23). S = -0.505 +/- 0.005 is for the forced runs F11 to F27, R_lambda about 28.5 to 82.9 (p. 15; Table 3, p. 35); the table also lists -0.502 at 9.0, -0.523 at 12.3 and -0.32, -0.40, -0.44 for decaying runs at 2.33, 4.07, 6.20. Kerr's compressive principal strain is the one of largest absolute value, in the 0.5 % of grid points sampled on the magnitude of the rate of strain (p. 23); the trace is zero.

The nominal factors l_EI = l0/6 and l_DI = 60 eta are the lecture's (assumed in the lectures without justification); every share, width and threshold of the chapter is conditional on them, on eps = u0^3/l0 with unit constant, on u' = u0 and on C = 1.5. They are not verified.

The identification of the jet station as homogeneous isotropic turbulence with u' = u0 is an assumption stated in the text; chapters 7 and 8 found that homogeneity and isotropy do not hold for the jet.
Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times; they locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Symbols kappa = 2 pi / l, kappa_EI, kappa_DI, l_EI = l0/6, l_DI = 60 eta, u_0, Re_0 from the slides.
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model (homogeneous fluctuation field, isotropy only where stated); continuation of the jet of chapters 6-8 and the atmospheric layer of chapter 5; u' = (2k/3)^(1/2).

sections.section: Energy and dissipation in a band of wavenumbers
sections.lecture_material: Band integrals k(ka,kb) and eps(ka,kb) (slide f0025); the lecture states that the derivation of the dissipation integral is not important now.
sections.teaching_construction: Proof that eps = 2 nu int kappa^2 E dkappa needs homogeneity and incompressibility but not isotropy; the dissipation spectrum D(kappa).

sections.section: The transfer rate through the inertial subrange
sections.lecture_material: T(l) ~ u(l)^2/tau(l), T_EI = T(l) = T_DI = eps (slides f0007, f0013).
sections.teaching_construction: Stationary flux balance T(kappa) = eps - eps(0,kappa) and its assumptions.

sections.section: Dimensional analysis fixes the form of the spectrum
sections.lecture_material: E(kappa) universal function of eps and nu above kappa_EI; E = C eps^(2/3) kappa^(-5/3) between kappa_EI and kappa_DI (slide f0025).
sections.teaching_construction: E = (eps nu^5)^(1/4) Psi(kappa eta); unique exponents; status of the hypothesis and of C.

sections.section: The measured spectrum: what collapses, where the power law holds, and which constant
sections.lecture_material: Slide Figure 6.14 (one-dimensional longitudinal spectra scaled with Kolmogorov variables; caption cites Saddoughi and Veeravalli 1994); the lecture reads the collapse as the first similarity hypothesis.
sections.research_extension: Saddoughi (1993) Figure 3 and pp. 245-250; Yeung and Zhou (1997) abstract, eqs. (1)-(3), Table I; the one- versus three-dimensional distinction and C = (55/18) C1.
sections.teaching_construction: Reading of the collapse as a high-wavenumber statement; comparison of C values and their spread; comparison of kappa_DI with the simulated inertial range.

sections.section: The convergence argument for the exponent
sections.lecture_material: E = A kappa^-p; k(kappa,inf) = A kappa^-(p-1)/(p-1) for p > 1; eps(0,kappa) = 2 nu A kappa^(3-p)/(3-p) for p < 3; p = 5/3 (slide f0035).
sections.teaching_construction: Critique: the conditions apply to an unbounded power law, not to the finite inertial range; per-logarithmic-interval reading of the exponents; Exercise 3.

sections.section: Where the energy and the dissipation lie
sections.lecture_material: k(kappa,inf) ~ kappa^(-2/3) and eps(0,kappa) ~ kappa^(4/3): bulk of energy at l > l_EI and bulk of dissipation at l < l_DI (slide f0046).
sections.teaching_construction: Integrals of the -5/3 law between the nominal limits, shares 7.6/9.0 % (jet) and 13.2/11.1 % (layer), bounds 13.3/11.1 %, effect on the flux balance.

sections.section: The hypotheses for the N-point density of velocity differences
sections.lecture_material: Definitions of local homogeneity and local isotropy and the three hypotheses for f_N (slides f0010, f0018).
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov (1941) Definitions 1 and 2 and the hypotheses of similarity, pp. 9-10 and 12.
sections.teaching_construction: Remark that a second-order statistic is one moment of f_2 and that the hypotheses constrain no one-point statistics.

sections.lecture_material: D_ij definition, independence of x0, isotropic form D_ij = D_NN delta_ij + (D_LL - D_NN) r_i r_j / r^2 (slides f0022, f0027).
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov (1941) eqs. (22)-(23), p. 13; Saddoughi (1993) p. 238 (C2 ~ 4 C1, third-order -4/5 law as quoted).
sections.teaching_construction: Proof of the isotropic form; D_LL = C2 (eps r)^(2/3) from the second hypothesis; C2 = 4.018 C1 from the cosine pair; the slide's typo in D_ij is corrected.

sections.section: The two-point correlation of isotropic turbulence: f, g and the integral scales
sections.lecture_material: R_ij = u'^2 [g delta_ij + (f - g) r_i r_j / r^2]; L11 = int f dr; L22 = int g dr = L11/2 (slides f0033, f0036, f0037, f0039).
sections.teaching_construction: Continuity relation g = f + (r/2) f'; proof of L22 = L11/2 with its tail condition; D_NN = D_LL + (r/2) dD_LL/dr and its limits 2 and 4/3.

sections.section: The Taylor microscales and the dissipation rate
sections.lecture_material: lambda_f = [-f''(0)/2]^(-1/2), lambda_g = [-g''(0)/2]^(-1/2), lambda_g = lambda_f/sqrt(2); Taylor (1935) eps = 15 nu u'^2/lambda_g^2 and its incorrect interpretation (slides f0042, f0046).
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov (1941) eqs. (11), (13), (14), pp. 11-12; Saddoughi (1993) pp. 237 and 242.
sections.teaching_construction: Proof of lambda_g = lambda_f/sqrt(2) and of eps = 15 nu <(du1/dx1)^2> from f and g; the jet and layer numbers showing that lambda_g is not the dissipative-eddy size.

sections.section: The large-scale, Taylor-scale and Kolmogorov scales
sections.lecture_material: L = k^(3/2)/eps, Re_L = k^2/(eps nu), lambda_g/L, eta/L, Re_lambda = (20 Re_L/3)^(1/2), lambda_g/u' = sqrt(15) tau_eta (slides f0050, f0055); the lecture's remarks that Re_lambda applies only to grid turbulence.
sections.research_extension: Saddoughi (1993) Table 1 and p. 242 (Re_lambda in a boundary layer); Yeung and Zhou (1997) abstract (Re_lambda > 140).
sections.teaching_construction: Algebraic proofs of the identities; running-case values; comparison of the nominal inertial-range width with measured and simulated ranges; grading of the lecturer's judgments.

sections.lecture_material: Definition S = <(du1/dx1)^3>/<(du1/dx1)^2>^(3/2) (slide f0055); no further discussion in the lecture.
sections.research_extension: Kerr (1983) p. 15 and p. 23 (value -0.505 +/- 0.005, no Reynolds-number dependence over a wide range, compressive principal strain).
sections.teaching_construction: Reflection-symmetry argument that S is not forced to zero, in contrast to odd moments of a transverse derivative.

sections.section: Executable checks: the spectrum integrals, the range shares and the isotropic relations
sections.teaching_construction: Program and its output; the nominal inertial-range width against Re_lambda.

sections.section: What the statements establish and what they do not
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov (1962) p. 84 eq. (10); Yeung and Zhou (1997) p. 1 on intermittency and the second-order exponent.
sections.teaching_construction: Statement of the status of each result and the conditions of each share and constant.

symbols_introduced.definition: Wavenumber associated with an eddy size by the slide's convention; wavenumbers of the demarcation lengths.
Energy and dissipation in a wavenumber band (slide notation k_(ka,kb), eps_(ka,kb)); dissipation spectrum 2 nu kappa^2 E(kappa).
Rate of energy transfer from modes below kappa to modes above it (wavenumber counterpart of T(l)).
Universal function of the first hypothesis; Kolmogorov constant of E(kappa); of E11(kappa1); of the longitudinal structure function (Kolmogorov 1941 writes C).
One-dimensional longitudinal spectrum and its wavenumber.
Amplitude and exponent of a general power-law spectrum (slide).
Position and velocity differences about a reference point; N-point density; domain (slide script G).
Second-order structure function tensor, longitudinal and transverse components (slide).
Longitudinal and transverse autocorrelation functions (always with the argument), longitudinal and transverse integral scales.
Longitudinal and transverse Taylor microscales; bare lambda = lambda_g.
k^(3/2)/eps, k^(1/2) L/nu, u' lambda_g/nu (slide R_lambda).
Velocity-derivative skewness (slide); chapter 7 writes mu_3-hat for a standardized third moment.

references.title: A. N. Kolmogorov, The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers (1941; translation Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 434, 1991)
references.supports: Second moments, B_nn = B_dd + (r/2) B_dd' (eq. 12), a_n^2 = 2 a^2 (eq. 13), eps = 15 nu a^2 (eq. 14), the two hypotheses, B_dd ~ C eps^(2/3) r^(2/3), B_nn ~ (4/3) B_dd and ~ 2 B_dd (eqs. 23-25)

references.title: A. N. Kolmogorov, A refinement of previous hypotheses concerning the local structure of turbulence ..., J. Fluid Mech. 13 (1962) 82-85
references.supports: Moments of the longitudinal velocity difference with the factor (L/r)^(chi p (p-3)/2)

references.title: S. G. Saddoughi, Local isotropy in high Reynolds number turbulent shear flows, CTR Annual Research Briefs 1992
references.supports: E11 definition, eps = 15 nu <(du/dx)^2> (see Taylor 1935), C = 55/18 C1, C2 ~ 4 C1, C2'/C2 = 4/3, third-order -4/5 law as quoted, no consensus on local isotropy in shear flows (p. 238); lambda and R_lambda definitions (p. 242); Table 1 (p. 243); -5/3 range of about two decades at R_lambda 1500 on the log-log plot and Figure 3 compilation (pp. 245-246); C = 1.5 +/- 0.1, bump, slightly less than one decade at R_lambda 600 (p. 247); more than one decade at R_lambda 1500 on the compensated plot, less than the log-log plot suggested (p. 249); v-spectrum, Reynolds number and the compensated linear-log plot as the test of an inertial range (p. 250); C2 = 2.0 +/- 0.1 from second-order structure functions (pp. 255-256)

references.title: P. K. Yeung, Y. Zhou, On the universality of the Kolmogorov constant in numerical simulations of turbulence, ICASE Report 97-64
references.supports: C1 and C in the one- and three-dimensional spectra, C = (55/18) C1 under isotropy (eqs. 1-3), Sreenivasan's survey 0.53 +/- 0.055, Zhou's C = 1.5, DNS C1 ~ 0.60 and C ~ 1.62, inertial range at k eta ~ 0.02-0.05 for R_lambda > 140, intermittency effect on the second-order exponent small

references.title: R. M. Kerr, Higher-order derivative correlations and the alignment of small-scale structures in isotropic numerical turbulence, NASA TM 84407 (1983)
references.supports: Velocity-derivative skewness -0.505 +/- 0.005 for runs F11 to F27 (R_lambda about 28.5 to 82.9) and its Reynolds-number independence; Table 3 values at lower R_lambda; negative skewness and compressive principal strain of largest absolute value
references.page_checked: pp. 15, 23 and Table 3, p. 35 (PDF pp. 17, 25 and 37)
